St Petersburg governor reports no victims after ‘large-scale’ overnight attack that also hit Baltic port of Vysotsk Ukraine launched a big overnight drone attack on St Petersburg and the surrounding area, hitting the city’s oil terminal and port infrastructure in the wider region. The St Petersburg governor, Alexander Beglov, said the city had been subjected to a “large-scale” drone attack that had hit its oil terminal. He said there were no casualties and the aftermath of the attack had been dealt with. Alexander Drozdenko, governor of the surrounding Leningrad region, said a drone had struck the area of Vysotsk port, about 170km (105 miles) north-west of St Petersburg on the Baltic Sea. The port handles oil, grain, coal and liquefied natural gas.

Ukraine has continued striking Russia with drones (Image: Ukrainian 93rd Mechanized brigad) Russian officials confirmed Saturday that a Ukrainian drone strike targeted an oil terminal in St. Petersburg, as Kyiv continues its relentless campaign against Russia's energy infrastructure. Near-daily long-range assaults on Russian oil facilities have triggered a fuel crisis and intensified political pressure on the Kremlin, as its full-scale invasion of Ukraine enters its fifth year. Governor Alexander Beglov reported that the city's Kirovsky district, situated on the Baltic Sea, bore the brunt of the attack. He further noted that air defense systems successfully intercepted 72 Ukrainian drones over Russia's second-largest city and its surrounding areas. Russia bombs out Red Cross center in Ukraine destroying 320,000 relief items US warns Poland of potential Russian armed provocation to test NATO's response

Drozdenko said 72 drones had been shot down over the region, and there was minor damage in several settlements. He gave no information on the impact on Vysotsk port. In a post on Telegram, the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, described the attack as part of Ukraine’s “long-range sanctions” against Russia. Zelenskyy said: “Ukraine’s defence forces struck port oil infrastructure that generates revenue for Russia’s war, and also hit Kronstadt, an important military target more than 850km (530 miles) from Ukraine’s state border.” The Russian president, Vladimir Putin, dismissed the strikes on energy facilities as “not critical”. There was no Russian confirmation of a strike on Kronstadt, a major naval base near St Petersburg that Ukraine also targeted in an attack last month.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
St Petersburg governor reports no victims after ‘large-scale’ overnight attack that also hit Baltic port of Vysotsk

Ukraine launched a big overnight drone attack on St Petersburg and the surrounding area, hitting the city’s oil terminal and port infrastructure in the wider region.

The St Petersburg governor, Alexander Beglov, said the city had been subjected to a “large-scale” drone attack that had hit its oil terminal. He said there were no casualties and the aftermath of the attack had been dealt with.

Alexander Drozdenko, governor of the surrounding Leningrad region, said a drone had struck the area of Vysotsk port, about 170km (105 miles) north-west of St Petersburg on the Baltic Sea. The port handles oil, grain, coal and liquefied natural gas.

Drozdenko said 72 drones had been shot down over the region, and there was minor damage in several settlements. He gave no information on the impact on Vysotsk port.

In a post on Telegram, the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, described the attack as part of Ukraine’s “long-range sanctions” against Russia.

Zelenskyy said: “Ukraine’s defence forces struck port oil infrastructure that generates revenue for Russia’s war, and also hit Kronstadt, an important military target more than 850km (530 miles) from Ukraine’s state border.”

The Russian president, Vladimir Putin, dismissed the strikes on energy facilities as “not critical”.

There was no Russian confirmation of a strike on Kronstadt, a major naval base near St Petersburg that Ukraine also targeted in an attack last month.

Ukraine has intensified strikes on Russian energy infrastructure this year, inflicting heavy damage on refineries and causing petrol shortages across the country’s 11 time zones.

Elsewhere, the governor of Russia’s Bryansk region and the Russian-installed governor of Crimea said drone strikes had killed one person in each region, with several more wounded.

South of St Petersburg, the governor of Pskov region said more than 30 drones had been shot down overnight. He reported minor damage and injuries, including at a factory in the town of Velikiye Luki.

Zelenskyy also denied Russian claims that the eastern city of Kostiantynivka had been captured by Moscow’s military.

Russia’s military told president Putin on Friday that its forces had taken control of the city, a target that the Kremlin has long sought in its advance through the Donetsk region.

payload.title: Ukrainan droonit iskivät Pietarin öljyterminaaliin ja Vysotskin sataman alueelle
payload.summary: Venäläisviranomaisten mukaan Ukraina teki laajan droonihyökkäyksen Pietariin ja Leningradin alueelle. Isku osui Pietarin öljyterminaaliin ja Vysotskin sataman alueelle, mutta kuolonuhreista ei raportoitu.
payload.content:
Ukraina teki yön yli jatkuneen laajan droonihyökkäyksen Pietariin ja sitä ympäröivälle Leningradin alueelle, venäläisviranomaiset kertoivat lauantaina. Pietarin kuvernöörin Aleksandr Beglovin mukaan hyökkäys osui kaupungin öljyterminaaliin, mutta uhreja ei ollut ja tilanteen jälkiseuraukset oli hänen mukaansa saatu hoidettua.

## Isku kohdistui öljy- ja satamainfraan

Beglov kuvasi hyökkäystä laajamittaiseksi. Hänen mukaansa Pietarin Kirovskin kaupunginosa, joka sijaitsee Itämeren rannalla, joutui iskun kohteeksi. Venäläisviranomaisten mukaan ilmapuolustus ampui alas 72 ukrainalaista droonia Venäjän toiseksi suurimman kaupungin ja sen lähialueiden yllä.

Leningradin alueen kuvernööri Aleksandr Drozdenko sanoi droonin osuneen Vysotskin sataman alueelle noin 170 kilometriä Pietarista luoteeseen Itämeren rannalla. Satama käsittelee öljyä, viljaa, hiiltä ja nesteytettyä maakaasua. Drozdenkon mukaan alueella kirjattiin vähäisiä vaurioita useissa asutuskeskuksissa, mutta hän ei kertonut tarkemmin, millaisia vaikutuksia iskulla oli Vysotskin satamaan.

## Kiova kuvaa iskuja pitkän kantaman pakotteiksi

Ukrainan presidentti Volodymyr Zelenskyi kuvasi Telegramissa hyökkäystä osaksi Ukrainan Venäjää vastaan kohdistamia ”pitkän kantaman pakotteita”. Hänen mukaansa Ukrainan puolustusvoimat iskivät satamien öljyinfrastruktuuriin, joka tuottaa tuloja Venäjän sodankäynnille.

Zelenskyi sanoi myös, että Ukraina osui Kronstadtiin, jota hän kuvasi tärkeäksi sotilaskohteeksi yli 850 kilometrin päässä Ukrainan valtionrajasta. Kronstadt on merkittävä laivastotukikohta Pietarin lähellä, ja Ukraina kohdisti sinne iskun myös viime kuussa. Venäjä ei vahvistanut Kronstadtiin kohdistunutta iskua.

## Iskut jatkuvat sodan viidentenä vuonna

Ukraina on jatkanut pitkän kantaman drooni-iskuja Venäjän öljylaitoksiin, kun Venäjän täysimittainen hyökkäyssota Ukrainassa on jatkunut viidettä vuotta. Lähteiden mukaan lähes päivittäiset iskut Venäjän öljykohteisiin ovat aiheuttaneet polttoainekriisin ja lisänneet poliittista painetta Kremliä kohtaan. Venäjän presidentti Vladimir Putin vähätteli energiakohteisiin tehtyjen iskujen merkitystä ja sanoi, etteivät ne ole kriittisiä.
